newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares close firmer, take Europe's lead.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares close firmer, take Europe's lead.

text.p: 1645 GMT - Shares closed firmed, taking their lead from the rest of Europe although utility group EDP continued to ease slightly under the weight of profit-taking.
*Operators said that the market could continue to advance on Thursday if the mood abroad remained positive. "Let's wait and see how the others do," said one trader.
*The banks were once more to the fore, with Banco Sotto hitting a new high for the year and its parent, insurer Mundial Confianca also closing strongly.

*Banco Sotto closed 3.14 percent higher at 1,480 escudos, just short of an earlier all-time high. Banco Comercial Portugues gained nearly two percent to 3,340 in very heavy trade of over one million shares.
*Traders said that non-residents, and one order in particular, were largely responsible for the stock's gains. It was recently upgraded to "outperform" by Schroders Securities.
*The advance of Banco Comercial, the second most heavily-traded share after EDP, coincided with a strong performance of the Spanish banking sector.
*Portugal Telecom was lifted by the performance of the stock in New York. The 3.2 percent gain to 7,197 escudos brought the share into line with its futures price on the Oporto Derivatives Exchange.
*Shares in wood to tourism group Inparsa hit successive highs due to optimism over the company's results for 1997 and for the first half results of its unit Sonae Industria, analysts said.
*The PSI-20 ended 1.28 percent higher at 7,352.31 points.
